newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit in range as dollar largely stays stable.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit in range as dollar largely stays stable.

text.p: The ringgit was trapped in its forecast range as the dollar was largely stable in Asian trading, dealers said.
There was also little incentive to trade with the market factoring in a possible 25-basis point hike in U.S. federal funds rate after Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
"Ringgit was caught in a tight range of 2.4765/90 as players stayed on the sidelines ahead of the FOMC meeting," said research house I.D.E.A.
"For now, there is talk of local corporates and U.S. names buying dollars at around 2.4760/65, while exporters' ringgit interest are suggested around 2.4820/25," it said.
The Singapore dollar fell against the ringgit after rising on Monday, with its near term outlook seen as bearish.
Dealers said a boost in U.S. rates will give more leeway for Malaysian to maintain its rates, thus underpinning the ringgit due to more attractive yields.
The Sing was at 1.7212/28 ringgit at the end of Kuala Lumpur trading at 1000 GMT, from 1.7231/50 on Monday. The ringgit was also at 2.4782/87 a dollar against 2.4795/05 previously.
